title: When Compilation Breaks Your GNN: A Numerical Stability Perspective

problem.claim: Deep learning compilers can introduce numerical instability in GNNs, causing divergence under hyperparameters that work in eager mode.

gap.claim: The interaction between compiler optimizations and GNN structure contributes to numerical fragility.

contributions.claim: The paper explains how reordered floating-point additions can produce amplified errors in ill-conditioned GNN computations.
The paper proposes Numerics-Aware Graph Compilation, which profiles per-aggregation numerical risk and selectively applies aggressive optimizations to well-conditioned operations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On Open Graph Benchmark datasets, NAGC preserves over 95% of compilation speedups, reduces numerical deviation by 10 to 100 times, and eliminates compilation-induced training failures.

narrative_sequence.summary: Compilation can destabilize GNN training despite working eager-mode hyperparameters.
Floating-point reordering interacts with ill-conditioned GNN aggregations, producing amplified rounding differences.
NAGC estimates numerical risk and limits aggressive optimization to well-conditioned operations.
Experiments report retained speedups, lower numerical deviation, and no compilation-induced training failures.

source_observation.claim: Compiler optimizations that reorder floating-point additions can be risky for structurally ill-conditioned GNN aggregations.

interpretation.claim: Numerical-risk-aware optimization may be preferable to uniformly applying aggressive compiler transformations.

application.claim: Profile numerical risk at the aggregation level and gate optimizations based on conditioning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported GNN compilation settings.

unknowns: The specific Open Graph Benchmark datasets and GNN architectures are not identified.
The profiling overhead, compiler baselines, hyperparameters, and numerical-deviation metric are not specified.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported results.
